title: AI Commercial Video Production: Buyer Guide
summary: AI commercial production can suit repeatable paid-social ads. Compare the creative brief, production method, rights and approved outputs before buying.
body_markdown:
## How do you turn an idea into a producible commercial?


Start with a sequence of communication jobs before choosing visual effects. Write what the viewer needs to understand at the opening, what evidence the middle supplies and what action the ending asks for. Then assign a production method to each job. This keeps a clever scene from consuming the project while the product remains unexplained.


For an illustrative meal-planning app, the opening might show the frustration of deciding what to cook. A fictional scene can communicate that feeling. The middle should show an authentic example of selecting meals in the app. The ending should describe the actual next step available on the destination page. A generated image of an impressive interface would be a poor substitute for a screen recording that proves the real workflow.


Build a shot ledger with columns for purpose, source, required accuracy, production method and approval owner. Mark anything that must stay exact, such as packaging, interface text or the order of a physical operation. A scene described only as “product magic” needs another discussion before it becomes a production commitment.


Once the ledger is complete, ask the supplier to identify the uncertain shots. Approve a simpler fallback for each one. The fallback should preserve the ad's meaning, such as replacing an unreliable hand interaction with real close-up footage. This gives the team a way to finish the brief without quietly changing the product claim.


## How should a commercial be designed for useful variations?


Decide which parts can change before producing the master. A modular plan can separate the opening situation, product proof and closing offer. The purpose is to make each variation answer a different question, not to multiply exports for their own sake.


For example, a fictional desk lamp campaign might explore a small-workspace use case and an evening-reading use case. Both can use the same approved footage of the actual lamp controls. Each needs a different opening and supporting context. Changing the entire product demonstration would add work without necessarily helping answer which situation is more persuasive.


Record the relationship between the assets. Label the underlying concept, the opening variation and the export format separately. If you request two concepts, three openings per concept and two aspect ratios, describe that as two concepts, six creative variants and twelve exports. Those are planning units for this example, not a recommended volume or a supplier's counting rule.


Have the editor check that the pieces still connect naturally. A reusable ending can become misleading if it refers to a benefit removed from a shorter edit. Review each finished version as its own ad, including the transition to the destination. Shared parts reduce repeated work only when their meaning remains intact.


## What happens when feedback arrives after production starts?


Classify the requested change before deciding how to handle it. A factual correction, a new creative direction and a newly introduced offer are different requests. The supplier and client should agree which requires correction within the original brief and which changes the brief itself.


Imagine a fictional bottle commercial. The approved script says the bottle holds 600 milliliters, but the final caption says 800. That is a correction against an existing approved fact. If the buyer now wants the commercial to promote a different bottle, the product, proof and destination may all need updating. Treating both changes as “one revision” leaves the real workload undefined.


Keep a short change log with the affected version, requested change, reason, approver and impact on delivery. Consolidate conflicting feedback before sending it to production. If one reviewer asks for a slower explanation and another asks for a shorter ad, resolve the communication priority rather than asking the editor to guess.


Review the first corrected version before applying the change across the batch. That is particularly useful when the correction touches a repeated caption, product shot or offer. A small approval step can prevent the same misunderstanding from spreading through every export.


## How should the commercial connect to campaign management?


A finished commercial still needs a launch decision. Agree which offer, destination and campaign context it belongs to, then name the person who confirms the final asset before use. Keep a record of which version actually ran so later feedback refers to the correct file.


Knowlify offers end-to-end Meta ads, combining creative production with campaign management. You can also commission creative only and retain your own buyer. Define the chosen responsibilities in the written scope; pricing is provided privately and media spend is separate. Neither arrangement requires you to turn a production deadline into a promise about campaign results.


For the first campaign review, ask what the commercial helped the team learn. Perhaps viewers responded to the product demonstration but the offer needs another explanation; perhaps delivery was too limited to form a useful view. Translate the supported observation into the next production question. Keep the approved product truth fixed while deciding which opening, proof or next step deserves another version.

## Key takeaways


- Choose methods according to what each scene must prove.
- Compare equal scopes, including revisions and rights.
- Approve the hardest shot early.
- Follow the[campaign brief](https://knowlify.com/articles/video-ad-campaign-brief) through final review.


## FAQ


### Are AI commercials always cheaper?


No universal saving is established here. Compare quotes for the same deliverables and include your team’s review time. A difficult generated scene can require a different production approach.


### Can AI replace a customer interview?


Do not present a fictional customer experience as real. Use the actual customer’s approved account when their experience is the evidence, and obtain the necessary permissions for its use.


### Can I use the same commercial on television?


Ask for the broadcaster’s delivery and clearance requirements before commissioning it. A paid-social scope should not be assumed to include broadcast specifications, music rights or distribution permissions.


### What should I provide to the production team?


Provide approved claims, accurate product assets, brand guidelines, intended placements, the destination and an approval owner. Identify scenes requiring authentic footage, then ask the producer to mark missing inputs and difficult shots in the scene ledger. Agree those decisions before approving the script so the chosen treatment is actually producible.
